brief.headline: Apollo Expands Daily Pricing to All Credit Assets, Advancing Transparency in Private Credit
bullets: Private Credit: In a press release: Apollo Expands Daily Pricing to All Credit Assets, Advancing Transparency in Private Credit.

M&A & Buyouts: CVC, Blackstone, Advent and EQT are among the potential bidders considering offers for Dutch drone detection specialist Robin Radar Systems, which could be valued at around €2bn in a sale by private equity owner Parcom, according to a report by Reuters.
Hedge Funds: Bridgewater Associates' flagship Pure Alpha fund gained 18.4% during the first nine months of 2026, compared with an average global hedge fund return of 7.25% cited by Morgan Stanley.
M&A & Buyouts: Blackstone said on October 1, 2026 that funds it manages will acquire Technology Service Corp. (TSC) and Applied Systems Engineering.
Private Credit: Apollo Global Management has begun rolling out daily pricing across its $850bn (£643.7bn) credit business as the industry tries to build a more transparent private credit market.
brief.marketRead: The S&P 500 stands at 7,666.45 (up 0.2% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 16.3, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.29% (up 3 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.46 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.12%, near long-run norms (up 4 bps on the prior reading). Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits.

items.title: Apollo Expands Daily Pricing to All Credit Assets, Advancing Transparency in Private Credit
items.takeaway: In a press release: Apollo Expands Daily Pricing to All Credit Assets, Advancing Transparency in Private Credit.
items.whyItMatters: Apollo is a private-credit heavyweight whose insurance arm, Athene, supplies long-term capital, which makes it central to the fusion of insurance and private lending. Developments here show how easily companies can borrow outside the banking system, and at what price. For allocators: private credit offers high floating-rate income but less liquidity, so manager selection and underwriting discipline matter.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.12%, near long-run norms (up 4 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 1.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.

items.title: Oaktree raises $2bn for debut asset-backed finance fund
items.takeaway: Oaktree Capital Management has raised $2bn for its first dedicated asset-backed finance fund, targeting lending opportunities outside the typical investment parameters of insurers, according to a report by Bloomberg.
items.whyItMatters: Oaktree, co-founded by Howard Marks, is a leading credit and distressed-debt investor whose views on risk cycles are followed across the industry. Big fundraises show where institutional money is flowing and hand managers fresh dry powder to put to work over the next few years. For allocators: watch which strategies are attracting capital, because crowded areas can compress future returns.

items.title: Europe faces $800bn annual infrastructure funding need, says KKR
items.takeaway: Europe needs between $700bn and $800bn of infrastructure investment each year, almost double current spending levels, with private capital expected to play a growing role in closing the gap, KKR’s co-head of European infrastructure Vincent Policard has said, according to a report by Bloomberg.
items.whyItMatters: KKR pioneered the leveraged buyout and now spans private equity, infrastructure, credit and insurance, so its activity is a barometer for global dealmaking. The AI build-out depends on power and data-center capacity, making infrastructure one of private markets' biggest growth stories. For allocators: infrastructure can diversify a portfolio, but deal sizes are large and access often runs through the biggest managers.
